title: Salonia - Antoninianus - SALONINA AVG - Roman Coin - IVNO CONSERVAT - Billion
description:
Roman Imperial Coin – Antoninianus of Salonina
 

 Roman Empire, AD 260–268


 Empress: Salonina (Cornelia Salonina)
 

 Authority: Gallienus
 

 Dynasty: Valerian Dynasty
 

 Reign period: AD 260–268
 

 Denomination: Antoninianus
 

 Mint: Rome, Italy
 

 Date: AD 260–268


 Composition: Silver (billon)
 

 Manufacture: Struck
 

 Diameter: 16.6mm
 

 Weight: 3.06g
 

 Die axis: Variable


 Obverse:
 

 Diademed and draped bust of Salonina, facing right, set on a crescent.
 

 Legend: SALONINA AVG


 Reverse:
 

 Juno standing left, draped, holding patera in right hand and sceptre in left; peacock at her feet.
 

 Legend: IVNO CONSERVAT


 Deity depicted: Juno


 References:
 

 RIC V, Salonina (2), no. 11
 

 OCRE canonical URI:
 
  https://numismatics.org/ocre/id/ric.5.sala(2).11
 

 Historical note:
 

 Salonina was the wife of Emperor Gallienus. Coins issued in her name frequently feature Juno, emphasizing protection, stability, and the welfare of the imperial household during the mid-third-century crisis.
